In misclassifications, such features can dominate model predictions due to high correlation with area and perimeter, leading to overfitting on noise.

Mean concavity is a known feature in breast cancer datasets reflecting the irregularity of tumor boundaries. High concavity is associated with malignant tumors and has biological relevance, making it a meaningful signal, not a spurious one.

In cancer datasets, it is often a derived feature influenced by noise or sampling variation and lacks a direct pathological link. It may serve as a spurious indicator because it behaves similarly across benign and malignant cases, especially when poor data quality or noise exists in the segmentation process.
